submission.justification: S2 (gradient-boosted classifier with all variables including jet substructure) gives the highest expected statistical-only significance at every working point tested: 4.07σ at 50%, 4.14σ at 55%, vs S1 3.35σ and S3 2.75σ at 50%, consistent with the 2025 summary (4.1/3.4/2.6). The S2 scan (30%: 3.78, 45%: 3.97, 50%: 4.07, 55%: 4.14, 60%: 3.92, 70%: 3.84) peaks broadly around 50–55%; differences within that plateau are likely comparable to MC fluctuations, so 50–55% are effectively equivalent. CAVEAT: all numbers are statistical-only. No project document assesses background-estimate robustness or systematic uncertainties. S2 relies on jet-substructure variables, which are typically the hardest to model in background MC, so the 'robust background estimate' constraint is unverified. Before selection freeze, the team should run a systematics-inclusive comparison (e.g. data/MC substructure validation in control regions and a data-driven background estimate); if S2's background estimate proves fragile, S1 (kinematics only, ~3.35σ) is the natural fallback.
